target.primary_claim_source: Chih-Yu Lee et al., Real-time Multi-instrument Autonomous Discovery of Novel Phase-change Memory Materials, arXiv:2605.18033v1, submitted 2026-05-18

grades.in_silico_coregionalized_vs_independent_: B+ primary-study evidence; C exact replay

supported_scope: The paper demonstrates one live Mn-Sb-Te closed loop coupling XRD structural mapping and electrical-resistance optimization through a shared multi-output GP posterior while using distinct acquisition objectives for the two instruments.

The paper reports 25 closed-loop iterations in about 5 hours and a headline seven-fold speed-up, and separately reports retrospective in-silico comparisons of coregionalized versus independent GPs and BO versus random sampling over the fully mapped 177-point library.
The in-silico comparison uses 10 sets of randomly initialized starting points and reports faster/more stable convergence for the coregionalized strategy on this dataset.
scope_limits: The physical demonstration is one material system and one live campaign; Figure-4-style comparisons are post-experimental simulation on the completed library, not repeated physical-lab replications.

The seven-fold headline is not an isolated ablation of cross-output sharing. The manuscript elsewhere describes at least/about five-fold acceleration versus conventional random sampling/throughput, so comparator and metric must be stated explicitly rather than treating 7x as a single universal orchestration effect.

paper_specification_strength: XRD measurement time is specified as 15 minutes per point (three 5-minute frames); resistance measurement is about 1.5 minutes per point (three approximately 30-second measurements).

The methods specify scikit-learn NMF with random initialization and a fixed random seed, StandardScaler normalization, GPy linear coregionalization with one latent function/rank 1 and Matern-3/2 kernel, and 5000 hyperparameter optimization iterations.
The paper states that some custom Python integration code and hardware-control/data-communication/computation code are available on GitHub and references a live-run recording.
replay_gaps: The preprint text inspected in this audit does not expose a concrete author-linked repository URL or immutable code revision; targeted public GitHub searches did not surface an exact author-linked MAD repository.
The numerical value of the fixed NMF seed is not specified in the paper text inspected here.
No immutable dependency/environment lock, exact Figure-4 seed list, raw 177-point benchmark bundle tied to the paper run, or raw per-seed Figure-4 output bundle was recovered in this audit.
Therefore the paper gives a strong method specification but not an exact historical replay contract.

measurement_cost_scheduling.candidate_hypothesis: schedule heterogeneous instruments using their actual measurement costs/latencies
measurement_cost_scheduling.paper_evidence: The demonstrated MAD architecture does not implement this. The paper says the faster process idles while waiting for XRD, MAD distributes time uniformly across tasks, and the single central kernel enforces equal numbers of data points across tasks. Asynchronous independent instrument servers are presented as a future mitigation.
measurement_cost_scheduling.audit_conclusion: Do not cite MAD as direct evidence that cost-aware/asynchronous scheduling improved the reported result. The 15-minute versus 1.5-minute asymmetry is a motivation and observed bottleneck, not a tested scheduling intervention.

dynamic_correlation_admissibility.candidate_hypothesis: suppress, shrink, admit, or revoke cross-output sharing when correlation support is weak
dynamic_correlation_admissibility.paper_evidence: MAD uses a rank-1 shared coregionalized model with task-specific residual variance and acknowledges that shared-model benefit is not universal when task correlations are weak. It does not report a dynamic model-selection/admission/revocation gate between shared and independent transfer during the live loop.
dynamic_correlation_admissibility.external_boundary_evidence: Multi-output GP literature independently establishes that negative transfer can occur when outputs lack common structure and motivates selective/regularized sharing.
dynamic_correlation_admissibility.audit_conclusion: The negative-transfer boundary is externally supported, but the candidate's dynamic admissibility gate remains an O-specific/downstream adaptation hypothesis rather than a reproduced MAD component.

time_varying_structural_representation.paper_evidence: NMF is rerun as data arrive and the basis evolves; the paper explicitly warns that phase-resistance correlations are not directly comparable across iterations.
time_varying_structural_representation.audit_conclusion: Treat cross-output relation estimates as iteration-local unless an additional alignment/stability mechanism is supplied. This does not negate within-iteration coregionalization.

independent_replication.search_scope: Targeted searches for the exact paper title/arXiv id, reproduction/replication language, and distinctive Mn-Sb-Te result strings did not identify a protocol-matched third-party rerun.
independent_replication.interpretation: Absence in this search is not evidence of failed replication; the paper is recent and should remain primary-study evidence until a matched independent rerun is available.

failed_replication.scope_guard: No negative result was found that justifies generalizing against multi-output GPs, autonomous materials laboratories, or multi-instrument orchestration as a family.

o_specific_adaptation.boundary: These adaptations may be motivated by MAD and negative-transfer theory but must not inherit MAD's empirical performance claims without matched tests.

evidence_notes: Primary preprint arXiv:2605.18033v1 was checked for architecture, instrument timing, model specification, Figure-4 benchmark design, discussion limitations, and code-availability statements.

A third-party arXiv-text mirror/catalog was used only as a transport aid to inspect the paper text and as weak evidence that public code availability is partial; it is not treated as an official implementation or independent reproduction.
Targeted GitHub searches were used to look for an author-linked exact MAD implementation; no exact paper-run repository/revision was recovered.

Li-Kontar negative-transfer results are used only to support the general failure boundary for inappropriate multi-output sharing, not as evidence that MAD's candidate-specific gate was implemented or validated.

Exact seed values, dependency lock, 177-point benchmark data, and raw per-seed Figure-4 outputs become public.
A protocol-matched independent reproduction or failed reproduction appears.

A matched experiment dynamically admits/revokes cross-output sharing and compares it with always-shared and independent models, especially under correlation shift.
